introduction.en: The International Labour Organization (ILO), established in 1919, is the UN agency responsible for setting international labor standards and promoting social justice.
introduction.hi: The International Labour Organization (ILO), established in 1919, is the UN agency responsible for setting international labor standards and promoting social justice.

body.en: The ILO operates through a unique tripartite structure involving governments, employers, and workers. Its 'Decent Work Agenda' focuses on four pillars: employment creation, social protection, rights at work, and social dialogue. In a globalizing economy, the ILO plays a critical role in preventing a 'race to the bottom' by establishing universal standards that protect workers from exploitation while fostering sustainable economic growth.

overview.title: International Labour Organization
overview.definition: The International Labour Organization (ILO) is a specialized agency of the United Nations mandated to advance social and economic justice by setting international labour standards.
overview.importanceInUpsc: Frequently tested in UPSC Prelims regarding UN specialized agencies, core conventions, and India's ratification status. In Mains (GS Paper II/III), it is crucial for questions on labour reforms, informal economy, social security, and international governance.
learningOutcomes: Master foundational concepts and mechanisms of International Labour Organization.
Evaluate spatial distribution, institutional frameworks, and policy dimensions.
Apply high-yield mnemonics to solve tricky Prelims and Mains questions.
prerequisites: Core foundational concepts of International Relations and Indian Labour Economics

sections.title: Core Foundations & Conceptual Framework
sections.content:
• **Tripartite Structure**: Unique UN agency bringing together governments, employers, and workers representatives in its executive bodies.
• **Establishment & Nobel Peace Prize**: Created in **1919** by the Treaty of Versailles as an affiliated agency of the League of Nations; became the first specialized agency of the UN in **1946**. Awarded the Nobel Peace Prize in **1969**.
• **Headquarters**: Located in **Geneva, Switzerland**.
• **Key Metric / Factor**: Adopts international labour standards through **Conventions** (legally binding treaties when ratified) and **Recommendations** (non-binding guidelines).

sections.title: Comprehensive Classification & Comparative Matrix
rows: Cover core human rights at work: Forced Labour, Freedom of Association, Child Labour, Discrimination.
Mandatory for all ILO member States to respect, promote, and realize, even if not ratified.
High Prelims probability: India has ratified 6 out of 8 (notably missing C87 and C98).
Promote tripartite consultation, employment policy, and labour inspection.
Monitored regularly to ensure robust domestic labour administration frameworks.
Frequently confused by aspirants with fundamental conventions.
Sector-specific standards addressing maritime labour, safety, health, and specific industries.
Ratification depends on domestic legislative readiness and economic capacity.
Mains value addition for writing on occupational safety and gig economy.

items.definition: The 'Parliament of Labour' that meets annually in Geneva to set international labour standards and adopt the ILO budget.
The executive council of the ILO that meets three times a year in Geneva, making policy decisions and drafting the agenda for the ILC.
The permanent secretariat of the International Labour Organization, functioning as its operational headquarters, research center, and publishing house.
An integrated policy framework combining job creation, rights at work, social protection, and social dialogue.

items.title: Major Geographical Distribution / Regional Hubs
items.content:
• **Global Presence**: Operates through regional offices in Africa, Americas, Arab States, Asia and the Pacific, and Europe and Central Asia.
• **Decent Work Technical Support Teams (DWT)**: Decentralized hubs providing technical guidance and policy advisory services directly to member states.

items.title: Challenges, Reforms & Forward Strategy
items.content:
• **Bottlenecks / Issues**: High rates of global informal employment, rise of platform/gig economies, and uneven ratification of core conventions.
• **Policy Interventions**: India's recent amalgamation of 29 central labour laws into **4 Labour Codes** aligned with principles of ILO conventions on occupational safety, wages, and social security.

items.title: Mnemonic for India's Unratified Core Conventions
items.content:
• **Memory Acronym / Phrase**: "India CANNOT yet join 87 and 98"
• **Decoded Meaning**: India has NOT ratified ILO Convention **87** (Freedom of Association and Protection of the Right to Organise) and Convention **98** (Right to Organise and Collective Bargaining) due to domestic civil service conduct rules restricting union rights for government employees.
• **Prelims Exam Value**: Directly answers statements claiming India has ratified all 8 fundamental conventions.

items.title: Retention Rule of Thumb
items.content: • **Core Formula / Rule**: Out of 8 fundamental conventions, India has ratified **6** (Missing: 87 & 98). Out of 4 governance conventions, India has ratified **2** (C81 and C144).

upscNotes.content: Examiner Trap: UPSC frequently states that 'ratification of an ILO convention automatically makes it binding domestic law in India.' This is FALSE. International treaties require explicit domestic legislative enactment in India.
Mains Value Addition: Cite the ILO's 'World Employment and Social Outlook' report or 'Decent Work' framework while structuring answers on unemployment, formalization, and labor reforms.

keyTakeaways: The ILO is the sole tripartite UN agency uniting governments, employers, and workers.
India has ratified 6 out of the 8 fundamental ILO conventions, omitting Conventions 87 and 98.
Labour standards are established via Conventions (binding upon ratification) and Recommendations (non-binding).
